summary: Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, the French Institute of Pondicherry, Columbia University, Kyoto University, and the Clay Sanskrit Library.
Somboon Watana is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Panjab University in 1999 under the supervision of Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma.

Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara (1913–2013) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Vajirayanavangsa and Swami Satyananda Puri. He was Director at Mahamakut Buddhist University (1961), abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1961–2013), and Supreme Patriarch of Thailand (1989).
Somphong Santacitto is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master's degree in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat.

Sonam Chhoki works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed an MA at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a PhD at SOAS University of London, and served as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

Sonam Gyatso (born 1933) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko (~1962–1970) and was a Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).

Sonam Kachru is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold, and held positions at the Forum Transregionale Studien and the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science.
Sonam Kinga (born 1973) is a historian and Tibetologist. He studied at Sherubtse College and Kyoto University, and served as a researcher at the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH from ~1999 to 2007.

Sonam Thakchoe works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1999–2002) mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, and held a post there around 2008.

Sonam Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Gray Tuttle, having also studied under teachers including Khenzur Dawa, Drepung Khenzur Gyatso, Samdhong Rinpoche, Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Gyumé Khenzur Lobzang Trinlé.

Songeun Choe specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Myung-dae Moon for an MA, Choe earned a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Kiyohiko Munakata.

Sonja Arntzen (born 1945) is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of British Columbia (~1968–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, and also studied under Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

Sonja Glauch (born 1967) is a linguist who earned her Magister, Promotion, and Habilitation at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg. Her appointments include positions at Erlangen-Nürnberg, Heidelberg University Library, the University of Vienna, and the University of Munich.

Sonya S. Lee works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under Wu Hung, and held positions at Swarthmore College, Stanford University, and the University of Southern California.

Soonil Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at Dongguk University under Seungwon Seo, completed a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich, and later served on an editorial committee at Dongguk University.

Sophus Bugge (1833–1907) was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1858. He held posts at Uppsala University and the University of Oslo, where he became professor of comparative philology, comparative Indo-European linguistics, and Old Norse in 1866.

Soshuku Shibatani (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and Koyasan University (Master's and PhD), and held posts at Sonoda Women's University, Junrei Henro Kenkyukai, and Koyasan University.
Soshū Nishioka (born 1949) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at International Buddhist University.

Sotan Oka (1860–1921) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He served as professor, academic dean (1899), and president (1918) of Komazawa University, and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Soyen Shaku (1859–1919) was a Buddhist studies and religious scholar. He studied at Keio University and under Kosen Imakita, among others. He was Zen master at Engaku-ji (1892) and president of Hanazono University (1914–1917).
